questions.question: On a coordinate grid, Mia plots three points: (−3, 2), (0, 2) and (4, 2). She joins them with a straight line. Which equation describes her line?
options: y = 2x
questions.explain: Every point has the same y-value, 2, while x changes, so the equation is y = 2. Writing x = 2 is the common trap: that line is vertical, standing 2 units to the right of the y-axis.

questions.question: On a coordinate grid, Ravi draws the line x = −2. Which of these points lies on his line?
questions.explain: On x = −2 every point has first coordinate −2, so (−2, 6) is on the line. The point (6, −2) swaps the coordinates, and (0, −2) would sit on the horizontal line y = −2 instead.

questions.question: On a coordinate grid, a line passes through the points (5, −1), (5, 0), (5, 3) and (5, 7). Which statement about this line is true?
options: It is horizontal, and every point on it has y = 5
It is horizontal, and every point on it has x = 5
It is vertical, and every point on it has x = 5
It is vertical, and every point on it has y = 5
questions.explain: The first coordinate is fixed at 5 while y changes, so the line is x = 5 and it stands straight up and down. A fixed x-value never makes a horizontal line; horizontal lines have a fixed y-value.

questions.question: On a coordinate grid, the line y = 3 passes through (−4, 3), (0, 3) and (6, 3). Why does its equation contain y but not x?
options: The line is vertical, so it touches only the y-axis, leaving only y
The 3 is really an x-coordinate, so the equation should say x = 3
x is always 0 on this line, so x drops out of the equation
Every point has y = 3 but x can be anything, so x is not needed
questions.explain: A horizontal line has the same y-value at every point while x is free to be any number, so the equation only needs to say y = 3. The line is not vertical, and x is certainly not always 0: the points (−4, 3) and (6, 3) are on it.

questions.question: A table of values has x-values 1, 2, 3 and 4, and the y-value is 6 in every row. Which equation and graph match the table?
options: y = 6, a horizontal line 6 units above the x-axis
y = 6, a vertical line 6 units right of the y-axis
y = 6x, a slanted line passing through the origin
x = 6, a vertical line 6 units right of the y-axis
questions.explain: The y-column never changes, so the relation is y = 6, and a constant y-value makes a flat horizontal line at height 6. It is not vertical, and it is not y = 6x, because y stays at 6 instead of growing with x.

questions.question: Kai rides the bus in Vancouver and pays a flat fare of $3 no matter how many stops he travels. Let x be the number of stops and y the fare in dollars. Which line is the graph?
options: The vertical line y = 3
The horizontal line y = 3
The horizontal line x = 3
The vertical line x = 3
questions.explain: The fare y is always 3 while the stops x can be any number, so the graph is y = 3, a flat line 3 units up. Calling it x = 3 would mean he always rides exactly 3 stops, and y = 3 is never a vertical line.

questions.question: Priya knows that the point (−5, 2) is on a horizontal line. What is the equation of that line?
questions.explain: A horizontal line keeps the y-value fixed, and the y-coordinate of (−5, 2) is 2, so the line is y = 2. Using −5 takes the x-coordinate by mistake, and x = −5 would be a vertical line.

questions.question: On a trail map drawn on a grid, Trail A is the line x = 4 and Trail B is the line y = −1. At which point do the two trails cross?
questions.explain: The crossing point must satisfy both equations: its x-coordinate is 4 and its y-coordinate is −1, giving (4, −1). Writing (−1, 4) swaps the coordinates, and dropping the negative sign puts the point on y = 1 instead.

questions.question: A delivery drone over Kamloops holds a steady height of 12 m for its whole flight. Time t in minutes is on the horizontal axis and height h in metres is on the vertical axis. What does the graph look like, and which points are on it at 4 min and 9 min?
options: A horizontal line h = 12, through (4, 12) and (9, 12)
A horizontal line t = 12, through (4, 12) and (9, 12)
A vertical line h = 12, through (12, 4) and (12, 9)
A slanted line h = 12t, through (4, 48) and (9, 108)
questions.explain: Height is the vertical-axis variable and it never changes, so the graph is the horizontal line h = 12, and every point has second coordinate 12. A steady value is not a steady rate, so h = 12t is wrong, and a line at one fixed height cannot be vertical.

questions.question: Liam is asked to graph x = −2. He marks −2 on the y-axis and draws a line straight across the grid, left to right, through that mark. What went wrong?
options: Nothing is wrong; an equation with only x in it is drawn straight across the grid
He drew y = −2; x = −2 is an up-and-down line through −2 on the x-axis
Nothing is wrong; x = −2 means the second coordinate of every point is −2
He should have gone through −2 on both axes, because x and y must be equal there
questions.explain: x = −2 says the first coordinate of every point is −2, so the line stands vertically through −2 on the x-axis. A line drawn straight across through −2 on the y-axis is y = −2, the opposite line.

questions.question: Ava checks a Surrey outdoor pool: it is 27 °C at 1 pm, 27 °C at 2 pm and 27 °C at 3 pm. She plots hours after noon as x and temperature in °C as y. If the pattern continues, which equation fits, and what does it give for 5 pm?
options: x = 27, so the pool is still 27 °C at 5 pm
y = 27x, so the pool is 135 °C at 5 pm
y = 27, so the pool is still 27 °C at 5 pm
y = 27, but the graph never reaches x = 5
questions.explain: The temperature y stays at 27 while the time x changes, so the relation is y = 27, and extending that horizontal line to x = 5 still gives 27 °C. A horizontal line reaches every x-value, and x = 27 would wrongly say the time is always 27.

questions.question: On a school map, four bike-rack posts are at (3, −2), (−2, 3), (3, 7) and (7, 3). A fence runs straight up and down through exactly two of the posts. Which two posts does it pass through, and what is the equation of the fence?
options: (3, −2) and (3, 7), on the line y = 3
(−2, 3) and (7, 3), on the line y = 3
(−2, 3) and (7, 3), on the line x = 3
(3, −2) and (3, 7), on the line x = 3
questions.explain: An up-and-down line keeps x fixed, so look for posts sharing a first coordinate: (3, −2) and (3, 7) both have x = 3, so the fence is x = 3. The posts (−2, 3) and (7, 3) share a y-value, so they lie on the horizontal line y = 3 instead.
